checks_actual_results: Updated stale database upgrade README to list V19/V20 and manifest example databaseVersion from 34 to the actual Flyway V20.

Deployment preflight now reads actual MySQL Flyway history, rejects failed history and version regression, verifies contiguous migration entries in the JAR against manifest databaseVersion, and requires a source-version-matched four-artifact backup before an existing database or configuration version advances. PreflightOnly returns readiness before any release directory or pointer is created.

Physical backup script now records databaseVersion=20 and configVersion=local-v1 with a real MySQL dump (11,336,098 bytes), file archive, configuration snapshot and reference-only secret plan; deployment checked file sizes, SHA-256, source version, database identity, environment and consistency point.

Against the real preview database, current V20→V20 read-only preflight returned READY twice. An isolated Flyway V19 history with a V21 fixture package rejected missing backup, accepted a complete backup, rejected a tampered configuration artifact, and rejected an injected failed Flyway migration. A configuration-only local-v1→local-v2 fixture also required the source-version backup.

On failed deployment after the database advances or configuration changes, the script now keeps the service stopped and writes FAILED_REQUIRES_RECOVERY with version, backup and forward-fix/restore directions instead of attempting to start an incompatible prior release. No production migration or release switch was executed in this substep.

After backend restart, MySQL flyway_schema_history reported V20 and zero failed rows; operations continuity API returned runtimeDatabaseVersion=20, runtimeConfigVersion=local-v1, and unprivileged member received 403. The admin page reopened with Flyway V20. PowerShell parser, workspace-validate and targeted git diff --check passed.
